name: Cinemas of India
description:
This elective course introduces the studies on Indian Cinema that foreground the South Asian region with a focus on film and cultural studies. The following theoretical approaches, topics and themes will be taught in the course, along with a student project on Indian Cinemas.
• Indian Cinemas: Introduction and Theory
• Bollywood and the Hindi Film
• Regional Cinemas
• Themes and Perspectives
• The Business of Indian Cinemas
• Cinema Experience and Audiences
• Student Projects
The course would discuss and illustrate arguments, and establish a broader understanding and relationship of an up-to-date critical narrative on diverse topics in cinema studies such as spectators, gaze, camera-look, censorship, film distribution, film industry, diaspora, sexuality, caste and gender, film music, language and identity, national and regional. It would provide a comprehensive and cutting-edge survey of Indian cinemas discussing popular, parallel/new wave, and regional cinemas, as well as the spectacular rise of Bollywood. The whole course would map around 4 to 6 films that accentuate these themes in the modules.
